item.title: Women should enter Parliament based on service, not gender - Adi Finau
item.description: Women should not seek a place in Parliament simply because they are women, but because they have built a record of service and have something meaningful to contribute. This has been highlighted by Soqosoqo Vakamarama iTaukei president Adi Finau Tabakaucoro while speaking to fijivillage News on women's participation in leadership and decision-making spaces.
item.content:encoded:
Women should not seek a place in Parliament simply because they are women, but because they have built a record of service and have something meaningful to contribute.

This has been highlighted by Soqosoqo Vakamarama iTaukei president Adi Finau Tabakaucoro while speaking to fijivillage News on women's participation in leadership and decision-making spaces.

Adi Finau says political representation must be backed by commitment, experience and a proven connection with communities.

Insert: Adi Finau - Service to the community July 06

She pointed to Minister for Environment Lynda Tabuya as an example of someone who has built recognition through community service .

While representation is important, she says more attention is needed on development issues that directly affect people's daily lives, including access to water, sanitation, healthcare and economic opportunities.

She says communities are often focusing heavily on discussions around rights, democracy and parliamentary representation, while basic needs and livelihood opportunities required greater attention.

Adi Finau says addressing these issues is a key focus of the Soqosoqo Vakamarama iTaukei's Strategic Development Plan 2025–2030, which aims to strengthen the organisation and empower women across Fiji.

The organisation has membership across all 14 provinces, 159 communities and 1,192 villages, and operates as a charitable trust.

She says a major focus of the plan is improving economic empowerment so women and communities could become more self-sufficient.

On domestic violence, Adi Finau says addressing the issue required a stronger focus on enforcement, adding that violence against women should be treated as a criminal matter.

S he acknowledged existing Government social protection programmes but says organisations such as Soqosoqo Vakamarama did not have the resources to replace government services.

Adi Finau says empowering women requires more than awareness alone, with greater emphasis needed on creating opportunities for communities to improve their livelihoods.

item.title: Claims sugar industry will collapse are nonsense - Kamikamica
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica has assured sugarcane farmers in Seaqaqa that Fiji's sugar industry will not collapse, following concerns raised during a public consultation. item.content:encoded:
Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica has assured sugarcane farmers in Seaqaqa that Fiji's sugar industry will not collapse, following concerns raised during a public consultation.

Responding to a farmer's concern that growers had heard claims the sugar industry was collapsing, Kamikamica described those claims as nonsense and stressed that if the sugar industry was collapsing, Government leaders, including Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka, would not be travelling to meet farmers and discuss ways to revive the sector.

Kamikamica says the presence of Government ministers, the Leader of the Opposition and representatives from other political parties showed that the sugar industry is a national issue rather than a political one.

INSERT: Kamikamica on sugar industry 6th Aug

Kamikamica acknowledged that there had been many previous attempts to address the industry's challenges, including numerous reports over the years, but stressed that the current Government is determined to ensure meaningful action is taken.

He says the Government believes there is a future for the sugar industry and is focused on finding practical solutions to strengthen it.

item.title: From rubbish to reward: Nadi piggery farmer Petero Senianitu turns recycling into extra income
item.description: What many people see as rubbish, Nadi resident Petero Senianitu sees it as an opportunity. A part-time driver and piggery farmer, Senianitu has been collecting recyclable plastic bottles and aluminium cans for the past three years.
item.content:encoded:
What many people see as rubbish, Nadi resident Petero Senianitu sees it as an opportunity.

A part-time driver and piggery farmer, Senianitu has been collecting recyclable plastic bottles and aluminium cans for the past three years.

Senianitu is taking advantage of he Government's Retun and Earn initiative where people trade clean plastic PET bottles and aluminum cans of any brand for 5 cents per container.

He says he collects recyclables to keep his community cleaner while earning extra money to support his family.

With the cost of living continuing to rise, Senianitu says finding alternative ways to earn an income has become increasingly important.

He says just two trips to a collection point with bags of empty bottles and cans can earn him close to $50.

He says the extra cash goes straight back into his piggery business, helping him purchase mill mix and other supplies needed to care for his livestock.

Senianitu says he hopes more people will see discarded bottles and cans not as waste, but as something with value.

item.title: VOU Fiji's Fijian Flying Circus set to showcase Fiji's culture across Australia
item.description: The Pacific's most internationally toured contemporary dance company will bring its unique blend of acrobatics, dance, storytelling, music and Fijian humour to audiences in Darwin, Brisbane, Melbourne and Sydney from August 2026 to January 2027. The tour follows two consecutive invitations for VOU to perform at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York and the company's achievement in becoming th
item.content:encoded:
The Pacific's most internationally toured contemporary dance company will bring its unique blend of acrobatics, dance, storytelling, music and Fijian humour to audiences in Darwin, Brisbane, Melbourne and Sydney from August 2026 to January 2027.

The tour follows two consecutive invitations for VOU to perform at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York and the company's achievement in becoming the first Fijian company to headline a major New Zealand arts festival in early 2026.

VOU Fiji says ticket proceeds contribute towards the Conservatorium of Dance, Fiji's first accredited tertiary dance qualification, which provides 20 young Fijians each year with a fully funded two-year diploma in Performing Arts, including accommodation and living support during their studies.

They say every graduate from the programme is guaranteed full-time employment with the VOU Fiji Dance Company, and the organisation currently employs more than 80 Fijians in the creative arts, with women making up the majority of its leadership roles.

VOU Fiji Director Sachiko Soro says the organisation's vision is to create opportunities for young Fijians to access quality creative education and build sustainable careers.

Soro says VOU Fiji trains young performers to an elite international standard so they can confidently represent Fiji on the world stage, while sharing Fijian cultural storytelling through circus, dance, acrobatics and humour.

VOU Fiji says presented by Fiji Airways and supported by Neptune Pacific, the Fijian Flying Circus will showcase Fiji's culture through raw acrobatics, aerial performances, traditional and contemporary dance, and indigenous storytelling inspired by Fijian myths and legends.

VOU Fiji says the Fijian Flying Circus began unexpectedly after its contemporary dancers crossed paths with touring circus trainers who stayed on to train alongside the performers.

They say with access to a spare circus tent, what started as an experiment developed into Fiji's first and only professional circus, combining circus skills with Fijian storytelling.

The organization says what makes the production unique is its spirit, with performances built around Fijian warmth, humour and the joy of human connection.

The Australian tour will include performances in Darwin from 20th to 22nd August at the INPEX Sunset Stage in Festival Park, followed by Brisbane from 4th September to 4th October at South Bank's Piazza.

The tour will then continue to Melbourne from 17th October to 22nd November at Melbourne Showgrounds, before concluding in Sydney from 12th December 2026 to 10th January 2027 at Blacktown Showgrounds.

Beyond entertainment, VOU says the tour supports its wider mission of creating sustainable opportunities for young Fijians through the creative arts.

Founded in Suva in 2007, VOU has performed in more than 35 countries and continues to promote Fiji's culture internationally through its performances.

They say its recent achievements, including its appearances at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York in 2025 and 2026 and its historic appearance at the Hamilton Arts Festival in New Zealand, reflect the growing recognition of Fijian creative talent globally.

item.title: Family, sporting icons gather to honour Olympian Simione Kuruvoli Snr
item.description: Family, friends, and members of Fiji's sporting community gathered at the Nabua Methodist Church on Sukanaivalu Road to honour former Olympian judoka Simione Kuruvoli Senior during his final church service. Among those paying their respects were rugby sevens legend Waisale Serevi and former Commonwealth Games gold medalist Ratu Nacanieli Takayawa.
item.content:encoded:
Family, friends, and members of Fiji's sporting community gathered at the Nabua Methodist Church on Sukanaivalu Road to honour former Olympian judoka Simione Kuruvoli Senior during his final church service.

Among those paying their respects were rugby sevens legend Waisale Serevi and former Commonwealth Games gold medalist Ratu Nacanieli Takayawa.

Kuruvoli Snr also leaves behind a proud sporting legacy through his grandson, FIJI Water Flying Fijians halfback Simione Kuruvoli.

Originally from the Mataqali Rukuruku, Yavusa Tiliva of Nabouwalu, Ono, Kadavu, Kuruvoli Snr survived by his wife Rosanna, six children, 24 grandchildren, and nine great-grandchildren.

item.title: More people to be questioned as Police verify alleged attempted child abduction claims at Nausori school
item.description: Police are verifying claims of an alleged attempted child abduction at a school in Nausori after a social media post identified a man, who has denied the allegation, lodged a counter-report against the woman who made the post, and says he was at the school to see his daughter. Following the circulation of the social media post, Nausori Police carried out initial enquiries and confirmed that invest
item.content:encoded:
Police are verifying claims of an alleged attempted child abduction at a school in Nausori after a social media post identified a man, who has denied the allegation, lodged a counter-report against the woman who made the post, and says he was at the school to see his daughter.

Following the circulation of the social media post, Nausori Police carried out initial enquiries and confirmed that investigations are continuing to establish the facts.

Police say more people are expected to be questioned as part of the investigation.

They have also confirmed that the man identified in the social media post has lodged a counter-report against the woman who made the allegation.

The man told Police he had gone to the school to see his daughter and not for the reasons claimed in the social media post.

He says he only became aware of the allegations after family members alerted him when they saw the post online, prompting him to lodge the report.

Police say the counter-report is also subject to the ongoing investigation.

They are stressing that investigations must be given time to be conducted properly and should not be rushed.

We have sent questions to Police to confirm whether the man's daughter attends the school and are awaiting their response.

The Fiji Police Force is urging members of the public to report incidents directly to Police and allow investigators to carry out their work before drawing conclusions.

Police are also reminding the public that the 1681 toll-free number can be used to report crimes, suspicious people or activities, as well as complaints against Police and concerns about service delivery.

item.title: From teacher to trailblazer: Rupeni Rokoratu builds a Fijian fragrance brand
item.description: Creating a proudly Fijian perfume brand capable of standing alongside the world's finest fragrances was a mission. This was shared by the founder of Perfume Fiji, Rupeni Rokoratu.
item.content:encoded:
Creating a proudly Fijian perfume brand capable of standing alongside the world's finest fragrances was a mission.

This was shared by the founder of Perfume Fiji, Rupeni Rokoratu.

The former high school teacher stepped away from his career with a vision to create a proudly Fijian perfume brand capable of standing alongside the world's finest fragrances.

After eight years of dedicated research and development, Perfume Fiji became a reality.

Rokoratu says his perfume is crafted using natural ambergris and sikeci oil, ingredients traditionally valued by Fiji's ancestors.

He says his signature fragrance combines indigenous knowledge with world-class craftsmanship, creating a uniquely Fijian scent with global appeal.

He says his product is now proudly stocked at Tappoo Fiji, reaching customers both locally and internationally.

The former teacher adds that the brand is also preparing to expand into Papua New Guinea this September, marking another significant milestone in its growth.

Rokoratu's entrepreneurial journey was not without challenges, as access to funding remained one of the biggest obstacles until a 2025 grant from the iTaukei Trust Fund Board (TTFB) helped transform years of research into a successful commercial venture.

Reflecting on his journey, Rokoratu shared a simple but powerful message to dream big, but take action.

He says if people start today, they will get somewhere, but if they only dream and never act, they will never achieve their goals.

The iTaukei Trust Fund Board says that by supporting entrepreneurs like Rokoratu, it continues to fulfil its mandate of empowering iTaukei people through enterprise development.

The Board says that by investing in innovation, entrepreneurship and indigenous talent, it is helping to create sustainable economic opportunities that contribute to the long-term economic empowerment of the iTaukei community.
